skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-chatgpt-ads-ltv-bidding
skill.description: Set up customer lifetime value bidding for WooCommerce in ChatGPT Ads with Product Metrics. Verify which revenue or profit events arrive from paid orders before choosing a campaign conversion.
skill.summary: Configure and verify WooCommerce lifetime value tracking for ChatGPT Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are Markdown, documentation links, or normal setup guidance, with no evidence of malicious reconnaissance or reviewer-directed prompt injection. Confirmed risks involve external tool execution, remote tool access, and an unpinned installer. The workflow can also expose an API key, enable broader data sharing than expected, and send users to the wrong conversion event.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the exception for collecting API keys in chat or passing them as command values. Require direct entry in the verified Product Metrics interface or use a write-only secret field.
Require approval before using the remote connector or installing software. Verify the CLI path and publisher, and pin the installer version and skill revision.
Confirm the intended company and store before reading account data. Query only the authorized test order and report delivery and value without customer identifiers.

remediation.issue: Live conversion and customer data sharing
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling live sending, confirm the store, pixel, consent configuration, and approved event and data scope. Explain that enabling the destination can send more than LTV events.
Use bundled, reviewed references for operational steps. Treat external pages as informational and verify the destination before forwarding a tool-provided browser link.
Use pm_profit_ltv for profit LTV and pm_revenue_ltv for revenue LTV. Describe both as per-order contributions, and verify the intended event before changing the campaign.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Handling Conflicts With No-Chat Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The agent rules allow accepting the OpenAI Conversions API key and passing it to a command. The connection guide instead says never to paste it into chat. Agent inputs, tool traces, or process arguments could expose the credential before the destination stores it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception and the conflicting no-chat warning are explicit. No evidence shows a secret-safe input channel for the command path.

semantic_findings.title: Live Destination Sends More Than LTV Events
semantic_findings.description: The connection step leaves live sending on before the LTV guide explains consent. The destination also sends standard conversion events and customer matching data. The setup does not require the merchant to review that broader scope before activation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly leaves sending enabled and documents identifiers including IP address. It describes consent controls, so this is not evidence of consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Documentation Can Replace Reviewed Setup Steps
semantic_findings.description: When bundled references are absent, the agent is told to use live Markdown as equivalent operational guidance. Changes to those pages could alter credential or account setup steps without a change to the audited skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback substitutes live pages without a revision or integrity check. No evidence shows that the remote pages contain malicious instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Order Profit Event Misidentified as Profit LTV
semantic_findings.description: The main guide names pm_order_profit in its LTV workflow. The LTV reference names pm_profit_ltv for lifetime profit. A merchant following the main guide could optimize ad spend for order profit instead of the intended LTV event.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The references assign distinct purposes to these events. Manual campaign selection reduces immediate impact but does not correct the misleading instruction.

content.user_title: Set Up WooCommerce LTV Bidding in ChatGPT Ads
content.value_statement: A first purchase does not show how much revenue or profit repeat customers bring. Use Product Metrics to track what each paid order adds and verify the lifetime value conversion before selecting it in ChatGPT Ads.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status to identify which connection steps remain.
Guide a store administrator through installing the WooCommerce plugin and verifying live order delivery.
Explain the Pixel ID, consent, and destination settings needed for server-side conversion tracking.
Identify which cost settings are needed before Product Metrics can send profit LTV events.
Help verify receipt of a paid test order and identify the revenue or profit LTV event for manual campaign selection.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, an editor or admin role, a compatible WooCommerce store, and access to ChatGPT Ads Manager.
LTV uses observed orders from recognized customers, with marketing and analytics consent. It does not predict customer value.
Profit LTV requires known costs for the order. A loss-making order contributes zero profit value.
ChatGPT Ads does not import historical orders or revise sent events after refunds. It accepts events up to seven days old.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first revenue LTV campaign
use_cases.description: Check whether the store and pixel are connected. Validate the revenue LTV event from a test order before selecting it in Ads Manager.

use_cases.title: Compare revenue and profit signals
use_cases.description: Check whether order costs are complete. Choose an LTV conversion that matches the campaign objective.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing LTV conversions
use_cases.description: Check paid status, customer recognition, consent, and delivery for a test order before changing tracking settings.

prompt_templates.title: Explain LTV bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: the store owner is evaluating LTV bidding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain revenue and profit lifetime value bidding for my WooCommerce store. List the prerequisites without connecting any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check connection readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: the merchant has a Product Metrics workspace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup for my confirmed WooCommerce store and Product Metrics property. Keep this read-only, and tell me what I need to do in each app.

prompt_templates.title: Verify one paid test order
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: the merchant placed a test order after connecting the pixel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check delivery for my test order in the confirmed store. Report which LTV event arrived and whether costs or consent blocked another event. Omit customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a profit LTV pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: profit tracking is ready for campaign validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the profit LTV event for my confirmed test order. Suggest a starting target for one campaign, explain the assumptions, and leave campaign changes to me.

output_examples.input: Why is revenue LTV available but profit LTV missing for my test order?
output: Product Metrics received the paid test order, and the revenue LTV event arrived.
Profit LTV was not sent because a product cost was missing.
Set the missing cost, then place another test order before choosing profit LTV in Ads Manager.

output_examples.input: Which conversion should I select to bid on lifetime profit?
output: Choose pm_profit_ltv, not the order profit event.
Confirm that a paid test order produced the event before you select it in Ads Manager.
Select it yourself in one campaign and verify the selected conversion before adjusting the target.

best_practices: Enter the Conversions API key directly in the verified Product Metrics interface. Keep API keys and setup tokens out of chat.
Confirm the store, pixel, data scope, and consent settings before enabling live event delivery.
Verify the intended LTV event with one paid test order before selecting it in one campaign.
anti_patterns: Do not choose order profit when the campaign objective is lifetime profit.
Do not copy a purchase conversion target without reviewing how the LTV event measures value.
Do not bypass consent checks to make a missing test event appear.

faq.question: What does an LTV event contain?
faq.answer: It contains the revenue or profit contribution from one paid order. It is neither a prediction nor a full lifetime total sent with each purchase.

faq.question: Why might a paid order have no LTV event?
faq.answer: The customer must be recognized by account ID, email, or phone. The shopper must also grant marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Why is profit LTV missing when revenue LTV arrived?
faq.answer: Profit LTV requires all order costs. Revenue LTV can arrive without them, and a loss-making order contributes zero profit value.

faq.question: Will previous orders count toward LTV in ChatGPT Ads?
faq.answer: The LTV setup does not backfill previous orders to ChatGPT Ads. The platform accepts events up to seven days old.

faq.question: Can the assistant select my campaign conversion?
faq.answer: No. The assistant can guide setup and verification, but you select the conversion and value optimization in Ads Manager.

faq.question: Does the connection send customer information?
faq.answer: With marketing consent, events may include hashed identifiers and fields such as IP address and postal code. Review the data scope before enabling delivery.
